records.name: Nord-Ovest
records.summary:
This region hosts the country's first and second practical civic gender-recognition schemes: Milano's "registro di genere" - chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges, created by a 2022 council motion brought by the country's first elected transgender councillor - and Torino's analogous "Identita Alias" practice at the municipality and the public libraries. For a gender-nonconforming visitor these determine whether a ticket window or municipal desk becomes an argument.

Against this, the 2012-2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence names this region's two leading regions among the country's six highest-victim regions.

sources.summary: LifeGate: Milan inaugurated Italy's first gender registry ('registro di genere'), letting transgender people use their chosen name on civic and municipal documents — presented as a milestone for transgender rights in the country; the record ties it to a 2022 council motion by the country's first elected transgender councillor, with Turin's parallel 'Identita Alias' practice at municipality and libraries.

Progetto Gionata region-and-city aggression breakdown 2012-2025: source for this record's claim that the region's two constituent regions rank among the country's six highest-victim regions for anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence.

records.name: Nord-Est
records.summary:
The region's dominant constituent authority carries a documented record of official acts of hostility toward trans people. In 2014, following a council deliberation, the regional government formally instituted a mandatory "Natural Family Day" on the last school day before the Christmas holidays and rejected the aims and content of the WHO Regional Office's Standards for Sexuality Education in Europe, committing to deploy every available instrument against their adoption in the region's schools (official regional bulletin, December 2014).

In July 2018 the regional council approved a further motion pledging support for "those who fight in defence of the natural family" and for natalist policies, attacking the civil-unions law, and dismissing Pride marches as "carnival farces". These official acts create a clearly unwelcome climate signal; neither imposes a criminal sanction, fine or enforcement exposure on a visitor.

sources.summary: Regional council records: motion n.340 passed at the 178th public session in Venice (3 July), alongside deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 approving the motion that committed the regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' observance on the last school day before Christmas — the documented official-hostility claim of this record.

Official regional government bulletin (deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014): primary-source text of the Veneto regional council motion instituting the 'Natural Family Day' school observance and rejecting the aims of gender-awareness content — the record's central hostility claim in official form.
